$comment: GH-642 (queue item 6, stage 0b) - THE ONE LIST OF WHAT A CALCULATION NEEDS.
The owner's decision, 23.09.2026: 'there will be a list of the input parameters we
need for the calculation. The wizard will look at it, the calculation will look at
it, so that we do not put different checks in different places.'
ONE FILE, ONE READER. The server reads this; the wizard, Settings, the run and the
incomplete-run panel get it parsed, the way `analysis-result.schema.json` is already
read by the server and never copied into `assets`. A second list is the drift this
file exists to remove.
WHAT IS NOT HERE, AND DELIBERATELY:
- 'what breaks without it'. Who reads an input is what the dependency graph says;
restating it here would be a second answer to that question.
- the readings of a sample, one by one. Their names are declared once, by the lab
name map (`sample-manager.js`, `readingKeysFor`); an entry points at it.
- anything derived rather than asked: the climate regime, the purpose, the time
zone, the effective species. Those are named in `derived` below so the equality
test can exclude them BY NAME, with a reason, instead of by a rule.
`required: null` MEANS THE OWNER HAS NOT DECIDED, and it travels with `decision`.
It is not a guess and not a default: a warning built from this list stays silent
about such an input until she answers.
Contents drafted by the analyst (`PLAN-calculation-inputs-RU.md`, sections 14 and
14a) from a reading of the tree and the database, 22-24.09.2026.

$comment: GH-656 (queue item 6, stage 0b, slice 1) - THE VALUE DICTIONARY LIVES IN THE
ENTRY, because a value dictionary is part of declaring the input. The physical
tables stay in the engines; this says only which row of each consumer's table a
construction corresponds to.
EVERY `resolves` BELOW WAS READ OUT OF THE CONSUMER'S OWN TABLE, not decided
here, and `null` means that consumer's table does not carry the value - today it
substitutes something instead, and what it should mean is an owner's decision
still open. A `null` is therefore a measurement, not a gap in this file.
`offeredFor` IS ABSENT ON PURPOSE. Which constructions are offered to which turf
type changes the list a person sees in Settings, so it is the owner's; it travels
as `offeredForDecision` until she answers, the same way `required: null` does.
WHAT IS NOT DECLARED HERE AND WHY: `wearSandBased` and `preEmergentTexture` are
stated as measured, but their tables are not loadable on their own - one is a
list inside a minified engine, the other a comparison inside the orchestrator.
The equality test says so by name instead of pretending it checked them.
turf.construction.offeredForDecision: owner: which constructions are offered to which turf type

$comment: GH-644 - names the run reads out of its own state that are NOT inputs. Each one
with what it is, because 'read but not in the list' has two very different
meanings and only one of them is a defect: a result another engine wrote, or a
fact derived from an input. Anything read and in neither this block nor the list
is an input nobody declared, and the equality test names it.
notInputs.turf.ambientDLI: a result: the ambient DLI engine writes it
notInputs.turf.dli: a result: the shade engine writes it
notInputs.turf.shade: a result: the shade engine writes it
notInputs.turf.pgrActive: a result: the PGR module writes it
notInputs.soil.ESP: a result: the salinity engine writes it
notInputs.climate.data: a result: the climate engine writes it
notInputs.site.ledAvailable: a result: the lighting step writes it
notInputs.site.country: derived from the coordinates, like `site.region` beside it
notInputs.pgr.gddThreshold: derived from the PGR product type -- a property of the product, not asked of anyone
notInputs.climate.historical: a result: the historical weather window the run fetches from the PGR application date and carries into the next pass (GH-589). Nobody enters it.
notInputs.turf.ambientDLISource: derived: which road the ambient DLI came by, written by the run beside `turf.ambientDLI`, which is itself a result

$comment: Not inputs: worked out from an input rather than asked for. Named one by one so

also excuse a real omission.

derived.effectiveSpecies: from the species and the overseed
derived.effectiveVariety: from the variety and the overseed
derived.turf.speciesFractions: from the species and the overseed
derived.turf.grassType: from the species, normalised to an engine key
derived.turf.speciesKey: from the species, normalised to an engine key
derived.turf.effectiveSpeciesKey: from the effective species, normalised to an engine key
derived.turf.baseSpecies: from the species, before the overseed is applied
